title: An efficient and cost-effective purification protocol for Staphylococcus aureus Cas9 nuclease
protocol: Transfer 5 ng of 8×His-TEV-SaCas9 plasmid to one tube of XJb (DE3) competent cells.
Mix together plasmid and bacteria by finger flicking.
Incubate the mixture on ice for 30 min.
Heat shock competent cells at 42°C for 1 min.
Cool the mixture on ice for 2 min.
Transfer 950 μL fresh LB broth to competent cells.
Grow bacteria for 1 h in a bacterial shaker at 37°C and 250 rpm.
Evenly distribute 100 μL bacterial culture on a LB agar plate supplemented with 100 μg/mL Carbenicillin.
Grow bacterial colonies overnight in an incubator at 37°C.
Select 2 bacterial colonies from LB (Lennox) agar.
Grow each colony in 3 mL LB (Lennox) broth with 100 μg/mL carbenicillin overnight at 37°C and 250 rpm.
Expand the overnight culture in a 50 mL LB broth with 100 μg/mL carbenicillin overnight at 37°C and 250 rpm.
Transfer 10 mL bacterial culture into 4 × 1 L terrific broth with 100 μg/mL carbenicillin.
Grow bacteria until an optical density of 0.6–0.8 is reached, shaking at 37°C and 250 rpm.
Induce 8×His-TEV-SaCas9 protein expression with 0.5 mM IPTG, 1.5 mM L-arabinose, and 0.5 mM MgCl2.
Shake for 30 h at 18°C and 250 rpm.
Harvest bacteria by centrifugation at 6,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant and resuspend cells in buffer A with 1 mM PMSF.
Freeze cells at −80°C until protein purification.
Lyse cells by freeze and thaw between liquid nitrogen and 37°C water bath 2 times.
Remove ribonucleic acids with benzonase at 37°C for 30 min (0.5 μL benzonase per 10 mL bacterial lysate).
Spin down the insoluble fraction at 15,000 × g at 4°C for 30 min.
Filter and degas soluble proteins via a 0.22 μm filter unit.
Set aside 100 μl protein lysate in a microtube labeled cell-free lysate.
Set up chromatography as demonstrated.
Equilibrate a 5-mL HisTrap high performance column with 25 mL ddH2O, followed by 25 mL buffer B, and then 25 mL buffer A at a rate of 2 mL/min using a syringe pump.
Load degassed samples through the HisTrap column via a syringe pump at a rate of 2 mL/min for protein purification.
Collect unbound proteins in a clean bottle.
Set aside 100 μL protein lysate from the flow-through in a microtube labeled "flow through".
Do not exceed 150 mL of precleared, degassed cell-free lysate per batch purification.
Wash off unbound proteins once with 50 mL buffer A and again with 50 mL of 20% buffer B (40 mL buffer A and 10 mL buffer B).
Collect washed-off proteins in a clean bottle.
Set aside 100 μL protein lysate from the wash-off in a microtube labeled "wash-off".
Elute 8×His-TEV-SaCas9 with 100% buffer B in 6 consecutive fractions, 5 mL per fraction.
Set aside 100 μL protein lysate from each fraction and label each tube with corresponding fraction numbers.
Analyze enriched 8×His-TEV-SaCas9 proteins on a 10% SDS-PAGE gel prepared in section D.
Dilute protein lysates from steps 12, 14, 15, and 16 in 4× loading dye + 100 mM DTT.
Load 20 μL sample mixture to each well on a 10% SDS-PAGE gel.
Start electrophoresis at 90 V before the dye front reaches the end of stacking phase (about 10–15 min).
Continue electrophoresis at 120 V for the running phase (45–60 min).
Remove the polyacrylamide gel from a gel case and soak in ddH2O for 5 s.
Visualize 8×His-TEV-SaCas9 proteins in a ChemiDoc imager with medium image size, protein gels stain-free setting, and exposure time of 45 seconds.
Combine fractions that contain 8×His-TEV-SaCas9 proteins and dilute with buffer C by 3 folds.
Equilibrate cation exchange chromatography column with 25 mL ddH2O, followed by 25 mL buffer D, and then 25 mL buffer C at the rate of 2.0 mL/min using a syringe pump.
Dilute combined protein lysate with 3× its volume in solution C.
Filter diluted lysate via a 0.22 μm syringe filter.
Load equilibrated column with filtered protein lysates at the rate of 2.0 mL/min using a syringe pump.
Collect flow through solution and set aside 100 μL for analysis (Flow through fraction).
Wash unbound proteins off the column once with 50 mL buffer C, then again with 50 mL of 20% buffer D (40 mL buffer C and 10 mL buffer D).
Collect wash off solution and set aside 100 μL for analysis (wash off fraction).
Elute 8×His-TEV-SaCas9 proteins using 30% buffer D (35 mL buffer C and 15 mL buffer D) in six consecutive fractions, each of 5 mL.
Set aside 100 μL protein lysate from each elution fraction for analysis and label tubes with corresponding fraction numbers.
Dilute protein lysates from steps 16, 21, 22, and 23 in 4× loading dye + 100 mM DTT.
Load 20 μL sample mixture into each well of a 10% SDS-PAGE gel.
Electrophoresis starts at 90 V for the stacking phase (about 10–15 min).
Increase voltage to 120 V for the running phase (45–60 min).
Remove the polyacrylamide gel from the gel case and soak in ddH2O for 5 s.
Visualize 8×His-TEV-SaCas9 proteins using a ChemiDoc imager with medium image size, protein gels application, and stain-free gel settings. Exposure time is set to gel activation at 45 s.
Combine fractions containing 8×His-TEV-SaCas9 proteins.
Filter purified 8×His-TEV-SaCas9 proteins through a 0.22-μm syringe filter.
Mix purified His8-SaCas9 proteins with Cas9 storage buffer in a 1:1 ratio.
Equilibrate an Amicon ultra-15 centrifugal filter unit with 10 mL of Cas9 storage buffer.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 3,000 × g.
Transfer 15 mL of 8×His-TEV-SaCas9 to the centrifugal filter unit and centrifuge at 3,000 × g, 4°C until 1 mL of solution remains.
Repeat the process until all 8×His-TEV-SaCas9 solution has been filtered.
Wash the filter unit with 15 mL of storage buffer and repeat this step 2 more times.
Transfer the retentate containing 8×His-TEV-SaCas9 proteins to a new microtube labeled purified 8×His-TEV-SaCas9 proteins.
Measure protein concentration via Bradford assays.
Dilute proteins to the final concentration of 5 mg/mL.
Test the enzymatic activity of purified 8×His-TEV-SaCas9 proteins.
Mix together digestion ingredients as outlined in Table 2, vortex, spin down, and incubate at 37°C for 60 min.
Heat inactivates enzymes at 65°C for 10 min.
Assess digestion results on a 1% agarose gel.
